comments.author: @mike-nc8zd
comments.text:
Some of the issues are the buyers too. I sold my condo last fall and an identical quality unit sold for $250k within a week. I took notice that it was probably a fluke with a somewhat ignorant buyer who didn't realize she could have purchased it for $240k. I sold for $237k and still made numerous concessions. I really did not have any issues selling otherwise. 

However, I also put $38k into the house to update the place throughout my 7 years living there. All of these things got replaced by professional contractors: new matching furnace/AC units, new water softener, new water heater, new basement window, new Trex deck, all new carpet, a fully remodeled bathroom, and right before I sold I put an updated electrical panel in due to changes in code even though I wasn't required to swap it out. Still, so many buyers simply expect the fixer-upper price at the completely remodeled quality, including all of the small perks like dimmer lighting, added lighting, and all stair treads being replaced. 

Buyers are completely right on people asking for 3% inflation on their house based on 2018-2023 data, but at the same time, buyers are asking for completely free remodeling on houses selling at conservative prices. As a seller, there's no winning with most buyers. In retail, they call this the "savings high" or the "bargain rush". People get off sexually when they think they got an amazing deal. This, in part, is why sellers want to start high.
